conclusions: Feature Opus+Sol and Haiku+Terra each found eight independently supported behavioral issues in this pilot; their coverage differs. Opus+Sol also retained two supported observations. Earlier winner selection preceded the later user-requested Haiku+Terra run.
Feature two-Codex synthesis retained four supported behavioral findings; main two-Codex retained five. This sample does not establish a general branch advantage.

All-Claude retained fifteen model findings: seven supported behavioral issues, three supported observations, one unmeasured optimization candidate, and four unsubstantiated/refuted claims. Raw count overstates demonstrated quality.
All-Claude uses Claude for synthesis/matching too, so this is not a reviewer-diversity-only comparison.
G and H reused a C independent review; measured times are incremental. Adding approximate reused-stage time gives G 1261s and H 1131s, not measured standalone runtimes.

Suggestion continuation I preserved all ten C comments and byte-identical analysis/matching. Six patches generated, four omitted; five patches individually and jointly accepted. One failed verification evidence validation after a setup failure and successful retry, blocking full automatic publication.
The smaller D continuation likewise preserved all three B findings, attaching two accepted patches. Suggestions did not filter away findings in either continuation.
One initial PR snapshot and one sample per condition cannot establish a reliable model ranking or exhaustive recall. No GitHub publication performed.
Haiku+Terra completed in 670.13 seconds versus Opus+Sol 1798.90 seconds; both used two fresh reviews. This is observed latency for one run, not a reliable speed benchmark.

Haiku+Terra retained eleven comments: eight supported behavioral issues, two unverified claims and one refuted claim. Its synthesis performed source inspection without executing focused verification tests.

New confirmed historical issues R27 (stale owner buffer on reopen) and R30 (failed combined-repair adoption) are preserved with reproductions. R28 remains unverified and R29 was rejected; neither is counted as a supported bug.

all_claude_audit.qualification: Several retained claims need narrower failure scenarios or safer corrections. In particular, do not ignore all owner messages, bypass repository selection, or preserve ready state after changed verification inputs.

verification_recovery_observation.reason: Verifier reported an initial temporary-directory setup failure, then passing checks after setting TMPDIR. The application rejects accepted=true when any recorded check failed. The finding and proposed patch remain saved; automatic publication remains blocked.

raw_verifier_result.evidence: p10 is fixed without companion edits. The fallback sends SIGTERM to the active backend; api.dispatch already installs cancellation handling that stops subprocesses and unwinds locks. Publication saves intent before sending and retains it as ambiguous on cancellation. Focused checks exercised the exact Emacs cancellation function and async callbacks for refresh, prepare, publish, and recovery. All subprocesses were reaped, locks released, and drafts/uncertain intent retained. Existing operation-ID cancellation also passed. Full Magit integration was not run because Magit is unavailable.

qualifications: F2 does not bypass review: queued tasks lose initial fixer invocation and separate repair allowance.
F5 is supported for known publication receipts. Blanket exclusion of all owner messages could conceal meaningful new feedback.
F8 is a supported routing edge case when repository context is absent, not general failure of explicit repository selection.

F13 is a distinct combined-repair failure: all tasks complete, so the task interruption guard does not apply. Plain resume lacks explicit adoption, but still performs combined review. It does not revive the refuted unreviewed-acceptance claim R22.
F3 stale mapping exists in source, but realistic PR-destination change and wrong push remain unverified.
F10 overlooks terminal failure detection by the shared process supervisor; earlier real-subprocess reproduction applies unchanged.
Synthesis used source inspection without executing focused tests; independent checks supplied the recovery and Emacs reproductions.
